en: to be distinguished; to be classified; to be divided

examples.en: This book is divided into three parts.
They are clothes that are easy to tell apart by color.
The two words are distinguished by how they're used.
The trash is sorted by type.
You can't tell them apart from appearance alone.
Work goes smoothly when public and private are kept separate.

explain: '~으로 구분되다'는 여러 부분으로 나뉘는 것, '~와 구분되다'는 다른 것과 달라서 알아볼 수 있는 것이에요. 비슷한 '구별되다'는 차이를 알아보는 쪽에 더 가까워요. 책이나 목록을 나눌 때는 구분되다를 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The documents are sorted by color.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나뉜 결과가 지금 그대로 있다는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a state in which things are already divided or sorted.

phrases.example: 두 색이 비슷해서 잘 구분되지 않아요.
phrases.en: The two colors are similar, so they are hard to tell apart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 것과 달라서 알아보기 어렵다고 할 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form used when something is hard to tell apart from another.

phrases.en: The twins can be told apart by their voices.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말로, 차이를 알아보는 쪽에 더 가까워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A close synonym that leans more toward recognizing a difference.

explain_en: Passive — things sorted into categories (종류별로 구분되다) ~으로 구분되다 means being divided into parts, and ~와 구분되다 means being told apart from something else. 구별되다 leans more toward noticing a difference. For splitting books or lists, 구분되다 is common.

t90.ax: The trash is sorted by type.

en: to guffaw; to roar with laughter

examples.en: Grandfather is laughing heartily watching TV.
The guests roared with laughter at a single joke.
The men sit around talking and laughing loudly.
Father was in a good mood and laughing all day.

examples.ko: 너무 껄껄거리지 말고 조용히 해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't guffaw so much and keep it down.
The sound of loud laughter reaches the hallway.

explain: '껄껄 웃다'를 한 동사로 말한 거예요. '-거리다'는 같은 동작이 이어진다는 느낌이 있어서 계속 크게 웃는 모습에 어울려요. 윗사람이 웃을 때는 '껄껄거리셨어요'처럼 높여요.

phrases.example: 삼촌은 재미있는 이야기를 하면서 껄껄 웃어요.
phrases.en: My uncle tells funny stories and laughs heartily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻을 부사와 동사로 나눠서 쓴 말이에요. 말할 때는 이쪽이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, split into adverb and verb. This version sounds more natural in speech.

phrases.en: Grandpa told old stories with a hearty laugh.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 웃으면서 다른 행동을 같이 한다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-며' it shows doing something else while laughing.

phrases.en: Dad guffaws while watching TV.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이 웃을 때는 '-시-'를 넣어요. 활용하면 '껄껄거리세요'가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-시-' when an elder laughs. The polite form becomes '껄껄거리세요'.

explain_en: Near-synonym of 껄껄대다; the -거리다 form of hearty, deep laughter, typically of older men (할아버지가 껄껄거리며 웃으셨다). Interchangeable with -대다. It is '껄껄 웃다' packed into one verb. '-거리다' gives a feel of continued action, so it suits ongoing loud laughter. For someone senior, use the honorific form, like '껄껄거리셨어요'.

t90.ax: Grandfather is laughing heartily watching TV.

en: to quack; to squawk; to yell

examples.en: The ducks quack on the pond all day long.

examples.ko: 그렇게 꽥꽥거리지 말고 차분히 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't yell like that; try speaking calmly.

examples.ko: 옆집 아이가 복도에서 꽥꽥거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The kid next door was screaming in the hallway, so I couldn't sleep.
Why are you yelling only at me since this morning?

examples.ko: 시장에서 아저씨가 꽥꽥거리며 물건을 팔고 있어요.
examples.en: A man at the market is shouting as he sells his goods.
My friend screamed when he saw his test result.

explain: 오리 소리에도 쓰지만, 사람이 시끄럽게 소리를 지를 때 쓰면 '왜 저렇게 시끄럽게 굴어' 하는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. '소리치다'보다 거칠게 들리니까 남에게 직접 쓰면 무례할 수 있어요. 비슷하게 '꽥꽥대다'도 있어요.

phrases.en: I can hear kids shrieking outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꽥꽥거리다'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때 조금 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 꽥꽥거리다, a bit more casual in speech.

phrases.en: Please don't shout in the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용히 하라고 부탁하는 말인데 거칠게 들릴 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A request to be quiet, but it can sound harsh.

phrases.en: I hear quacking from the pond.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 시끄럽게 나는 소리를 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -는, it describes a loud, noisy sound.

explain_en: It is used for ducks, but when applied to people it sounds negative, as if they are being noisy and annoying. It sounds harsher than '소리치다', so saying it directly to someone can be rude. '꽥꽥대다' is a similar word.

t90.ax: The ducks quack on the pond all day long.

examples.en: I tied the string loosely, so it keeps coming undone.

examples.ko: 나사를 느슨히 조이면 흔들릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you tighten the screw only loosely, it may wobble.
I tied my hair loosely and sat down comfortably.
Nowadays the rules are being applied loosely.

examples.ko: 줄을 느슨히 잡으면 놓칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you hold the rope loosely, you might drop it.

examples.ko: 마음을 느슨히 먹으면 일이 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you let your guard down, things don't go well.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '느슨하게'라고도 말해요. 반대말은 '팽팽히'나 '단단히'이고, 끈·나사처럼 물건뿐 아니라 규칙이나 마음가짐이 풀린 것에도 써요.

phrases.en: I tied my shoelaces loosely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and more common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: The screw came loose, so the chair wobbles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팽팽하던 것이 풀어졌을 때 쓰는 변화의 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses a change from tight to loose.

phrases.example: 규칙이 느슨해서 다들 잘 안 지켜요.
phrases.en: The rules are loose, so people don't follow them well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건뿐 아니라 규칙이나 분위기에도 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for rules and atmosphere, not just objects.

explain_en: Not tight or firm, like a knot or rule; neutral. In everyday speech people also say '느슨하게'. Its opposites are '팽팽히' and '단단히', and it applies not only to things like strings and screws but also to relaxed rules or attitudes.

t90.ax: Nowadays the rules are being applied loosely.

en: invincibility; being unbeaten; being without any failure

examples.ko: 그 팀은 홈경기에서 불패 기록을 이어 가고 있어요.
examples.en: That team is keeping up its unbeaten record in home games.

examples.ko: 이 감독은 시즌 내내 불패를 자랑했어요.
examples.en: This manager boasted of being unbeaten all season.
The saying 'real estate never loses' is now a thing of the past.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 열 경기째 불패 행진 중이에요.
examples.en: Our team is on a ten-game unbeaten streak.

examples.ko: 불패의 에이스가 드디어 첫 패배를 당했어요.
examples.en: The undefeated ace finally suffered his first loss.

examples.ko: 그 후보는 선거에서 불패 신화를 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: That candidate kept up the myth of never losing an election.

explain: '불패 신화', '불패 행진'처럼 정해진 말과 함께 자주 써요. 스포츠 기사나 경제 뉴스 제목에서 '○○ 불패'라고 많이 보여요. 반대로 지는 것은 '패배'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 팀의 불패 신화가 드디어 깨졌어요.
phrases.en: That team's undefeated legend was finally broken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랫동안 지지 않은 놀라운 기록을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an amazing long streak without losing.

phrases.example: 우리 팀은 열 경기째 불패 행진을 하고 있어요.
phrases.en: Our team is on a ten-game unbeaten run.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지지 않고 계속 이어 가는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes continuing without a loss.

phrases.en: That player boasts an unbeaten record this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번도 지지 않은 것을 자랑스럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone proudly has never lost.

explain_en: Unbeaten record, often sports or reputation (불패 신화) It is usually paired with set words like '불패 신화' and '불패 행진'. You often see '○○ 불패' in sports and economic news headlines. The opposite, losing, is '패배'.

t90.ax: Our team is on a ten-game unbeaten streak.

examples.ko: 그 가게의 영업 행태가 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The way that shop does business became a problem.

examples.ko: 요즘 젊은 사람들의 소비 행태를 조사했어요.
examples.en: We surveyed the spending patterns of young people these days.

examples.ko: 운전 중에 휴대폰을 보는 행태는 위험해요.
examples.en: Looking at a phone while driving is dangerous behavior.
If this kind of behavior continues, you lose trust.
I observed the behavior of animals for a long time.
The employees protested against the company's unfair conduct.

explain: '행동'은 한 번의 움직임에도 쓰지만, '행태'는 반복되는 모습이나 방식을 말할 때 써요. 그래서 '소비 행태', '영업 행태'처럼 많이 쓰고, 좋지 않은 모습을 말할 때가 많아요. 칭찬할 때는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.example: 그런 나쁜 행태는 이제 고쳐야 해요.
phrases.en: That kind of bad behavior needs to be fixed now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '행태'는 좋지 않은 모습을 말할 때가 많아서 '나쁜'과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: '행태' often has a negative sense, so it pairs naturally with '나쁜' (bad).

phrases.example: 그 회사는 계속 이상한 행태를 보여요.
phrases.en: That company keeps showing strange behavior.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반복되는 모습이 겉으로 드러날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a repeated pattern of behavior shows on the outside.
phrases.en_equiv: to show a pattern of behavior

phrases.example: 요즘은 사람들의 구매 행태가 많이 달라졌어요.
phrases.en: People's buying patterns have changed a lot these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 물건을 사는 방식을 말하는 짝말이고, 꼭 나쁜 뜻은 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing about how people buy things; it is not necessarily negative.

explain_en: Typical pattern of behavior, usually criticized, written (무례한 행태) '행동' can describe a single action, but '행태' is for a repeated pattern or way of behaving. It appears in phrases like '소비 행태' (spending pattern) and '영업 행태' (business practice), and often points to something undesirable. It is rarely used for praise.

t90.ax: The way that shop does business became a problem.

examples.ko: 여름 내내 밖에서 놀아서 얼굴이 가무잡잡해졌어요.
examples.en: I played outside all summer, so my face became tanned.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 피부가 가무잡잡하고 눈이 커요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has darkish skin and big eyes.

examples.ko: 가무잡잡한 얼굴에 하얀 이가 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: White teeth suit a tanned face well.
I went to the beach, and now my arms are tanned.
That child has darker skin but looks healthy.
It got sunburned and turned darker.

explain: 주로 피부가 조금 어둡고 검은 느낌일 때 써요. 센 느낌의 '까무잡잡하다'도 같이 쓰는데, 말하는 사람의 느낌에 따라 고르면 돼요. 피부색을 말하는 것이라서 다른 사람에게 쓸 때는 조심하는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: Your darkish skin looks healthy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사가 올 때는 '-ㄴ' 모양으로 바꿔서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, the word changes to the '-ㄴ' form.

phrases.en: My skin is not darkish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아니라고 말할 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say something is not the case.

phrases.en: I got a dark tan from the sun.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가무잡잡하다'보다 센 느낌이고, 뜻은 거의 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A stronger-sounding version with almost the same meaning.

explain_en: It is mainly used when skin looks a little dark. The stronger-sounding '까무잡잡하다' is used as well, so you can choose by feeling. Because it describes skin color, be careful when using it about other people.

examples.ko: 아버지 얼굴에 검버섯이 하나둘 생기기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Age spots started appearing on my father's face one by one.
My grandmother wears makeup to cover her age spots.
I had an age spot removal treatment at the dermatologist.

examples.ko: 검버섯은 나이가 들면 더 많아지기도 해요.
examples.en: Age spots can become more numerous as you get older.

examples.ko: 자외선을 피하면 검버섯 걱정을 덜 수 있대요.
examples.en: They say you can worry less about age spots if you avoid UV rays.

examples.ko: 검버섯에 바르는 크림이 있는지 약국에서 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked at the pharmacy whether there is a cream for age spots.

explain: 기미나 주근깨와 달리 주로 나이 든 사람의 피부에 생기는 짙은 반점을 말할 때 많이 써요. '검버섯이 피다', '검버섯이 생기다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: As I got older, age spots appeared on my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 나타났을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common phrase for when they first appear.

phrases.en: Age spots have bloomed on Grandpa's hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: '피다'는 버섯이나 꽃이 피는 것처럼 퍼져 나타난다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 피다 gives the feel of spots spreading out like a flower or mushroom blooming.

phrases.en: He has a lot of age spots on his face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상태를 설명할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used to describe a condition.

explain_en: Unlike '기미' or '주근깨', it is mostly used for dark spots on older people's skin. People say '검버섯이 생기다' or '검버섯이 피다'.

examples.ko: 동생은 머리카락이 굽슬굽슬해서 파마한 것 같아요.
examples.en: My younger sibling's hair is so curly it looks permed.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 굽슬굽슬한 갈색 머리가 귀여워요.
examples.en: That child's curly brown hair is adorable.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 제 머리는 더 굽슬굽슬해져요.
examples.en: When it rains, my hair gets even curlier.
My hair curls up, so it's hard to comb.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 굽슬굽슬하던 머리가 커서는 곧아졌어요.
examples.en: My hair, which was curly when I was little, became straight as I grew up.
My grandfather's beard is curly.

explain: 같은 모양을 '곱슬곱슬하다'라고도 하는데, 머리카락이나 털, 수염처럼 가늘게 꼬불꼬불한 것에 써요. 머리 모양을 말할 때는 '곱슬머리'라는 말도 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: My hair is curly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 더 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more common word with the same meaning.

phrases.en: Curly hair suits you well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 '머리'를 꾸미는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describing 머리.

phrases.en: My younger sibling's hair is curly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 머리카락이 꼬불꼬불한 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form for describing hair that is curly.

explain_en: Variant of 곱슬곱슬하다 with a heavier, bigger feel; less common everyday word for curly hair. The same shape can also be described as '곱슬곱슬하다', and it is used for fine, wavy things like hair, fur or a beard. For hair, it is also useful to know the word '곱슬머리' (curly hair).

examples.ko: 기능성 화장품은 피부 고민에 맞춰 나와요.
examples.en: Functional cosmetics are made for specific skin concerns.

examples.ko: 이 운동복은 땀이 빨리 마르는 기능성 소재예요.
examples.en: This sportswear is a functional fabric that dries sweat quickly.

examples.ko: 기능성 식품을 먹기 전에 성분을 확인하세요.
examples.en: Check the ingredients before eating functional foods.

examples.ko: 디자인보다 기능성을 먼저 보고 신발을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I chose shoes by looking at functionality before design.

examples.ko: 기능성 양말이라 오래 걸어도 발이 편해요.
examples.en: These are functional socks, so my feet are comfortable even after long walks.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 기능성이 뛰어나서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This bag is popular because its functionality is outstanding.

explain: '땀이 빨리 마르는 기능성 소재'처럼 보통 다른 명사 앞에 붙어 특별한 기능을 넣은 물건을 말해요. 혼자 '기능성이 좋다'고 하면 겉모양보다 쓰임이 좋다는 쪽이에요. '실용성'은 쓸모가 있는 정도이고, '기능성'은 특정 기능을 넣었다는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: My parents take functional health foods.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강에 도움이 되는 특별한 기능이 있는 식품을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Food with a special function for health.

phrases.en: I bought functional shoes that are comfortable to walk in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편하거나 쓰기 좋게 만든 물건 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before things made to be comfortable or useful.

phrases.en: This bag is very functional.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모양보다 쓰임이 좋다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it works well rather than just looks nice.

explain_en: It usually attaches to another noun, as in '땀이 빨리 마르는 기능성 소재', for items with a built-in special function. On its own, '기능성이 좋다' means it works well rather than just looks good. '실용성' is how useful something is, while '기능성' stresses a specific built-in function.

examples.en: My little brother is tall, so his nickname is Beanpole.
That tall guy over there is my uncle.

examples.ko: 꺽다리와 키 작은 친구가 늘 같이 다녀요.
examples.en: The tall guy and his short friend always go around together.
There are a lot of tall guys on the basketball team.
That tall guy bumped his head on the door frame.
When I was little, I got teased as a beanpole.

explain: 키가 큰 사람, 특히 키가 크고 좀 마른 사람을 장난스럽게 부를 때 써요. '키다리'도 비슷한 말이고, 반대로 키가 작은 사람은 '땅딸보'라고 놀리듯 부르기도 해요.

phrases.example: 우리 반 키다리는 농구를 정말 잘해요.
phrases.en: The tall one in our class is really good at basketball.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이에요. '키다리'는 키 큰 사람을 부르는 더 가벼운 말이고, '꺽다리'는 마른 느낌도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word. '키다리' is a lighter way to call a tall person, while '꺽다리' also suggests being lanky.

phrases.example: 그 모델은 다리가 길어서 꺽다리 같아요.
phrases.en: That model has long legs, so she looks lanky and tall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 키가 크고 날씬한 모습을 장난스럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Playfully describes someone tall and slender.

phrases.example: 제 꺽다리 친구가 높은 선반의 책을 꺼내 줬어요.
phrases.en: My tall friend got the book from the high shelf for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에서 애정을 담아 부를 때 어울려요. 처음 만난 사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when affectionately referring to a close friend. Avoid it with people you've just met.

explain_en: It playfully refers to a tall person, especially a tall and rather thin one. '키다리' is a similar word, and the opposite, teasingly, is '땅딸보' for a short person.

en: aquiline nose; hooked nose; Roman nose

examples.en: That actor's hooked nose is his charm point.
I take after my father, so I have a hooked nose.
Many of my friends worry about their hooked noses.

examples.ko: 코가 매의 부리처럼 휘어서 매부리코라고 불러요.
examples.en: The nose curves like a hawk's beak, so it's called a hooked nose.

examples.ko: 성형 상담에서 매부리코를 펴고 싶다고 말했어요.
examples.en: At the consultation, I said I wanted to straighten my hooked nose.
Glasses slide down easily on a hooked nose.

explain: 코끝이 아래로 휘어진 코를 말하고, 반대로 코끝이 위로 들린 코는 '들창코'라고 해요. 외모를 직접 말하는 표현이라 다른 사람에게 쓸 때는 조심하는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: There's a friend with a hooked nose in our class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 코 모양을 설명할 때 쓰지만 다른 사람에게는 조심해서 말해야 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a nose shape, but be careful when saying it about others.

phrases.en: This statue's nose has a hooked shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람뿐 아니라 조각상이나 그림의 코 모양을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can describe the nose shape of statues or drawings as well as people.

phrases.en: I have a hooked nose, so my glasses often slip down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 코를 설명하며 이유를 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form used when giving a reason about one's own nose.

explain_en: It describes a nose whose tip curves downward; the opposite, with an upturned tip, is '들창코'. Since it comments directly on someone's looks, be careful when using it about other people.

en: to be listless; to be lethargic

examples.en: Since morning, he answered in a listless voice.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어져서 그런지 오늘 표정이 맥없어요.
examples.en: Maybe because of failing the exam, your face looks listless today.

examples.ko: 맥없어 보여서 무슨 일 있냐고 물었어요.
examples.en: You looked so listless that I asked if something was wrong.
Worn out by the heat, his steps were weak.

examples.ko: 맥없던 아이가 간식을 먹고 기운을 차렸어요.
examples.en: The listless child perked up after eating a snack.
If you feel that drained, rest early today.

explain: 사람의 표정, 목소리, 걸음처럼 기운이 빠진 모습을 말할 때 써요. '힘없다'보다 축 처진 느낌이 강하고, 부사 '맥없이'와 함께 외워 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: He went home with listless steps.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기운 없이 걷는 모습을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe walking without energy.

phrases.example: 어제 잠을 못 자서 오늘 맥없어 보여요.
phrases.en: You look drained today because you couldn't sleep last night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습에서 기운이 없다고 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks like they have no energy.

phrases.example: 시험 결과를 보고 맥없는 표정을 지었어요.
phrases.en: He made a dispirited face after seeing the test result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실망해서 힘이 빠진 얼굴을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a face that has lost energy from disappointment.

explain_en: It describes a drained look in a person's expression, voice or walk. It feels more droopy than '힘없다', and it helps to learn it together with the adverb '맥없이'.

t90.ax: Worn out by the heat, his steps were weak.

examples.ko: 겨울에 모피 코트를 입은 사람이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people wore fur coats in winter.

examples.ko: 모피를 입지 않는 사람이 점점 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More and more people don't wear fur.
This shop sells only faux fur.
Fur is warm but hard to take care of.
Be careful not to let water touch the fur.

examples.ko: 할머니가 오래된 모피로 목도리를 만들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother made me a scarf out of old fur.

explain: 동물의 털가죽으로 만든 옷감이나 옷을 말할 때 써요. 진짜가 아닌 것은 '인조 모피'라고 하고, 동물 몸에 난 털은 그냥 '털'이라고 해요. 동물 보호 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I only wear faux fur clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물 털이 아닌 가짜 모피를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means fake fur, not real animal fur.

phrases.en: That fur scarf looks warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모피로 만든 물건 앞에 '모피'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 모피 before an item to say it is made of fur.

phrases.en: Fur clothes are hard to take care of.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모피로 만든 옷을 통틀어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This refers generally to clothes made of fur.

explain_en: It is used for cloth or clothing made from animal pelts. A non-real version is called '인조 모피' (faux fur), and the hair on an animal's body is simply '털'. It comes up often in talk about animal protection.

examples.en: My grandfather always goes for a walk wearing a beret.

examples.ko: 화가처럼 보이고 싶어서 베레모를 하나 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a beret because I wanted to look like a painter.

examples.ko: 이 베레모는 어떤 옷에도 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: This beret goes well with any outfit.
The wind blew hard and my beret came off.
The soldiers march wearing black berets.

examples.ko: 프랑스 사람은 다 베레모를 쓰는 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: I thought all French people wore berets.

explain: '모자'보다 훨씬 구체적인 말이에요. '쓰다'와 함께 '베레모를 쓰다'라고 해요. 화가나 군인의 모습이 떠오르는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 그 화가는 항상 베레모를 쓰고 그림을 그려요.
phrases.en: That painter always paints while wearing a beret.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모자는 '쓰다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Hats go with the verb 쓰다.

phrases.en: I took off my beret indoors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓴 것을 벗을 때 '벗다'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 벗다 to take off what you wear on your head.

phrases.example: 군인이 검은 베레모를 쓰고 서 있어요.
phrases.en: The soldier is standing wearing a black beret.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색깔을 앞에 붙여 모자 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the color in front to describe the hat.

explain_en: It is much more specific than '모자' (hat). Use it with '쓰다': '베레모를 쓰다'. It often brings to mind painters or soldiers.
